Settings

Default model for the team

Local AI DEFAULT

Any OpenAI-compatible server on your machine: Ollama, LM Studio, llama.cpp, Jan, vLLM. Nothing leaves your computer.

Opened this file straight from your folder? Your server must allow browser requests. Ollama: set OLLAMA_ORIGINS=* and restart Ollama (see Help). LM Studio: Developer → Server settings → turn on Enable CORS.

OpenAI DEFAULT

Uses your OpenAI API key, called directly from this browser.

Claude (Anthropic) DEFAULT

Uses your Anthropic API key, called directly from this browser.

Keys are stored only in this browser and sent only to the provider you choose. Ticked: they stay for 30 days from when you last entered one, then you paste them again. Unticked: they are forgotten when you close the tab. Each teammate can use a different model: open their chat, then Edit persona.

Looking for the TPT helper…

Set up the TPT helper (once on each computer)

  1. Download the helper and unzip it into a folder that can stay put, such as Documents.
  2. In Chrome, open chrome://extensions, switch on Developer mode (top right), click Load unpacked and choose the dv-tpt-bridge folder that has manifest.json directly inside it. Edge works the same at edge://extensions.
  3. Opening this office as a file from your computer? On the helper's card click Details and turn on Allow access to file URLs. Your GitHub Pages copy doesn't need this.
  4. Sign in at teacherspayteachers.com in the same browser, then reload this page.

Options

The helper reads your seller totals and product stats from the TPT Dashboard, using the TPT sign-in in this browser. For the inbox it also reads the public questions and reviews on your products. It never reads buyer emails or order details, it posts a reply only when you click Approve, and it only talks to teacherspayteachers.com and this page. TPT has no public API, so if TPT changes its dashboard the helper may need an update. Days follow TPT's US Eastern time.

The mic uses your browser's speech recognition (Chrome and Edge work best). Voices come from your operating system.

Chats, personas and stand-up notes are saved in this browser only.

How Digital Vector HQ works

  1. Click a teammate (or their name tag). The camera flies in and their chat opens. Esc flies back out.
  2. Ask Vector for priorities, New brief to hand a task to anyone, Stand-up to gather the whole team at the round table for updates and an action list.
  3. Every teammate reads the company brief (Settings → Company) plus their own persona, which you can edit from their chat.
  4. Drag to orbit, right-drag or two fingers to pan, scroll or pinch to zoom. Click the big screen to look at the studio board.
  5. Send files with the 📎 button, drag them onto the chat, or paste a screenshot: PDF, Word, PowerPoint, Excel, RTF, text and images. Claude and OpenAI read PDFs in full (layout and pictures included); local AI gets the text.
  6. Staff sit by department: Sales & Marketing, Audit, Research and Programming, each under its own sign. Move someone from Edit persona → Department.
  7. Staff do the work. Ask for a worksheet, lesson, audit or description and they hand back a file (Word, PDF, RTF, HTML). Attach your Word, PowerPoint, Excel or text file and ask for changes: they return your file with the edits made (tracked changes in Word). Every reply also has a save button.
  8. Customer inbox: $ → Inbox lists unanswered TPT questions and reviews. Grace drafts a reply; nothing posts until you click Approve and confirm. Audit a listing sends a live product to Leo, Priya, Jordan or Tom for a report.
  9. Live TPT stats show on the Studio Board, in the greeting card and in the $ panel once the TPT helper is installed (Settings → TPT live). Your staff see the same numbers, so you can ask them about sales.
  10. The team keeps its own routine: coffee runs, lunch, TV in the lounge, the copier, the vending machine, desk visits and huddles. Click anyone wherever they are and they stop to talk. Hover a name tag to see what they're up to.

Running a local model with Ollama

1. Install Ollama, then pull a model:
ollama pull llama3.1
2. Let this page talk to it, then restart Ollama:
Windows (PowerShell): 
setx OLLAMA_ORIGINS "*"
macOS: 
launchctl setenv OLLAMA_ORIGINS "*"
Linux: 
OLLAMA_ORIGINS="*" ollama serve
3. Settings → AI models → Local AI → Ollama preset → Load models → Test.

Alternative to step 2: serve this file from localhost instead of double-clicking it, e.g. python -m http.server in its folder, then open http://localhost:8000.

OpenAI or Claude

Paste your API key into its card, pick a model, press Test. The key stays in this browser.

Version . Not seeing a change you uploaded? Your browser is showing an older copy: close the tab and reopen the page, or add ?v=4 to the address.
